messages:
emma: Heads up: spike in Pending GPU pods in eu-west1a since ~08:05. eviction-rate and preemptions up.

raj: saw the dashboard. tiny-gang queue affected. scheduler logs show repeated `nodeAffinity` rejects and `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` even though nodes report available GPUs.

carla: checked node logs: CNI reports conntrack table full around same time (`nf_conntrack: table full`). kubelet briefly sets NetworkUnavailable on nodes, then clears.

emma: that transient NetworkUnavailable could make our affinity predicates treat nodes as ineligible during scheduling window, causing the gang scheduler to give up and trigger preemption.

raj: short mitigation: 1) canary bump nf_conntrack_max on two eu-west1a GPU nodes, 2) temporarily loosen affinity for non-prod small-gang jobs, 3) add a 20s network-ready grace to our scheduler predicate.

carla: ops-bot can you start canary?

ops-bot: initiating canary: apply sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288 to g-eu-a-11,g-eu-a-12 via daemonset. No drains.

emma: also adding runbook snippet for oncall: `ss -s` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count` are quick checks; bump if needed.

raj: i'll open a tiny PR to add `--net-ready-grace=20s` flag to our scheduling plugin and gate it by queue label. will test in staging.

carla: canary result after 10m: those two nodes show headroom and scheduled pending pods; attach/detach backlog cleared for jobs that land there. evictions reduced locally but cross-az reschedules still happening because scheduler shuffles remaining pods.

emma: long-term: increase conntrack baseline for GPU fleet, add scheduler grace for transient network flips, and audit small-gang affinity usage to relax where safe. quantify impact: eviction churn ~2 GPU-hours lost in spike.

ops-bot: canary completed with no regressions. scheduling wider rollout in 30m unless blocked.

emma: thanks team. raj post the PR link when available and carla please run affinity audit and paste counts here.
